name: employee-fatigue-pictograms
description: Visual check for #1013's non-working activity pictograms: stages three drillers at once so that at a single checkpoint tick, one (Bob, dispatched to a nearby target) is already RESTING at a living_quarters while another (Stan, dispatched to a farther target) is still WALKING toward the same building — the two states the issue exists to make visually distinguishable (Zzz vs a walking icon). Command-mode assertions pin this via pendingActionCount/collapsedCount alone (the state dump has no per-employee activity-kind field — SerializableGameState in src/console-api.ts, confirmed by reading it ahead of writing this file), so this scenario proves the ENGINE reaches the dual state deterministically; the actual pictogram rendering is only provable once #1013 lands and this file is re-run with --screenshots (dev-visual-testing's Visual Validation Protocol) — it cannot be proven at Red phase since EmployeePictograms.ts is still a stub.

steps.description: Ordered before any employee exists — the first idle hire below (Walt) auto-claims and builds it (#556), landing him right next to it once done, which is what makes his own later rest near-instant and keeps him out of the way of the Stan/Bob pair this file is actually about. (32,32) is flat ground at this seed — confirmed live; (10,10)/(50,50) are not.

Walt (#1) — builds the quarters above, ends up idle right beside it. Not part of the walking/resting pair; kept well above the warning threshold for the whole file by that near-zero-distance own rest cycle staying brief.
Stan (#2) — dispatched far below (48,48), the WALKING member of the pair at the checkpoint.
Bob (#3) — dispatched nearby below (38,34), the RESTING member of the pair at the checkpoint.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- same test-hook class as needs-collapse-visual's own dispatch steps (employees.ts's `dispatch` case comment). Sixteen tiles from Stan's spawn point -- travel(1/tick) + work(20 ticks, BASE_TASK_DURATION_TICKS) drains fatigue past the NEED_WARNING_THRESHOLDS.fatigue (25) crossing around cumulative tick ~81-82 (confirmed live against this exact seed/command sequence), after which the walk BACK to the living_quarters (16 tiles) is what the checkpoint below catches mid-flight.

Much closer than Stan's target -- Bob crosses the warning threshold and completes his short walk back to the living_quarters (confirmed live: fully arrived and resting by cumulative tick ~85, several ticks before Stan finishes his own longer walk back), so he is already RESTING while Stan is still WALKING at this file's checkpoint below.

expect.note: By tick 80 the living_quarters Walt built stands complete (buildingCount:1, no separate wait_until needed -- construction finishes well inside this batch), Bob has already crossed his warning threshold and is mid-walk-or-arrived, and Stan is still working/travelling. No one has collapsed (all three stay well above NEED_COLLAPSE_THRESHOLDS.fatigue=5 through this batch, confirmed live).

Cumulative tick 87 -- the checkpoint this whole file is staged for. pendingActionCount:2 is two live rest PendingActions (Bob's and Stan's own), confirmed live at this exact tick against this exact command sequence: Bob is already resting at the living_quarters (arrived ~tick 85, RestActionHelpers.ts's rest duration holds him there for NEED_REST_DURATIONS.fatigue ticks) while Stan is still mid-walk back from (48,48), not due to arrive until several ticks later -- exactly the walking_to_rest + resting pair #1013's pictograms exist to tell apart. Once EmployeePictograms.ts is implemented, re-running this file with --screenshots should show a Zzz icon over Bob and a walking icon over Stan in the same frame; state-dump fields alone (no per-employee activity-kind field exists in SerializableGameState) are as far as command mode can pin this without it. Staging a fourth employee through to an actual collapse in the same window was tried and abandoned -- the three-way stagger above is already tuned tightly enough (a handful of ticks) that adding a fourth trajectory reliably knocked the Bob/Stan overlap this file depends on out of alignment; the visual feedback loop that lands with the implementation is better placed to add a collapsed-pictogram checkpoint on its own terms.

steps.description: Textual confirmation of the three fatigue readings at the checkpoint -- Walt comfortably rested, Bob resting near the floor his rest will lift him from, Stan lower still and dropping (mid-walk).
